title: Quarterly strategic plan: Dedicated capacity resilience & autoscale playbook
creator: Riya Patel
description:
Objective: Deliver a repeatable quarterly playbook that reduces dedicated capacity over-provisioning by 30% while maintaining SLO compliance for tail latency and throughput. Scope covers policy design, SDK/API knobs, observability signals, and runbook for incidents.

Background: Customers buying Dedicated capacity ask for predictable throughput and cost transparency. Current behavior: teams set large reserved pools to avoid degraded tail latency during traffic spikes, increasing costs. Prior work (metrics collection + basic autoscale) exists but lacks operational playbook, SLO-aligned policies, and integration with Dedicated billing/quotas.

Key results (Q1):
- KR1: Cut reserved GPU hours for pilot customers by 25–35% through policy changes and cache-aware batching.
- KR2: Define and ship 3 autoscale policy templates (latency-first, cost-first, hybrid) documented in Console and API.
- KR3: Create an on-call runbook and rollback plan proven in one staged canary for a Dedicated customer.

Milestones:
- M1 (2026-01-31): Finalize policy designs, SLO mapping, and metric sets (p50/p95/p99 latency, queue depth, cold-start rate, evicted-KV-rate).
- M2 (2026-02-21): Deliver autoscale API additions + console UI for policy selection (canary mode).
- M3 (2026-03-15): Pilot with 2 mid-market customers; collect cost/latency delta and update templates.
- M4 (2026-03-31): Publish playbook, templates in Console, and internal runbook; hand off to Support + Solutions.

Deliverables:
- Autoscale policy spec (latency thresholds, cooldowns, burst windows).
- Console controls: policy selector, estimated cost delta preview, and historical simulation view.
- API: policy CRUD endpoints and policy evaluation logs.
- Playbook: incident runbooks, rollback steps, recommended quotas, and migration checklist for customers.

Acceptance criteria:
- Template policies reduce baseline reserved costs for pilot customers without violating p99 latency SLO > 99.5%.
- Console shows estimated cost delta within ±15% of observed delta during pilot.
- Support runbook validated by on-call drills and one live canary.

Risks & mitigation:
- Risk: Reactive autoscale may thrash during bursty workloads. Mitigation: cooldown windows + KV cache warmup signals + controlled ramping.
- Risk: Billing confusion when autoscale reduces reserved usage mid-cycle. Mitigation: Clear billing doc + billing preview in Console + backstop policies for committed capacity.

Metrics to track: p99 latency, tail failure rate, average reserved GPU hours per customer, cost per 1M tokens, autoscale invocation rate, and number of manual overrides.

Stakeholders: Product (Riya/Marcus), ENG runtime (lead: S. Nguyen), ENG infra (lead: Priya Rao), Design (lead: Elena Gomez), Solutions & Support.
